blocks.text: Jeremiah 25 places its warning in Judah’s transition from Josiah’s time into Babylonian domination. The chapter’s seventy-year announcement is associated with Babylonian rule and later restoration, and later readers interpreted that period in different ways. There is also a textual question behind the chapter’s list of nations: the Masoretic form of Jeremiah and the Old Greek form preserve markedly different ancient editions, with the Greek form shorter and placing the nation-oracles earlier in a different order.

Jeremiah 25 stands at the close of a large opening section of the book. The received book of Jeremiah brings together poetry, prose sermons, narratives, letters, headings, repeated accounts, restoration collections, nation-oracles, and an appendix; its present shape reflects a long compositional and textual history. This helps explain why the book should be read as a varied collection rather than as one uninterrupted speech or narrative.
